source.paper: CBSE Secondary School Examination 2025 - Mathematics (Standard) 041 - Marking Scheme
source.question: Q36

syllabus2026_27.note: AP nth term and sum are IN.

question.text: Case Study − 1: A school is organizing a charity run to raise funds for a local hospital. The run is planned as a series of rounds around a track, with each round being 300 metres. To make the event more challenging and engaging, the organizers decide to increase the distance of each subsequent round by 50 metres. For example, the second round will be 350 metres, the third round will be 400 metres and so on. The total number of rounds planned is 10.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Write the fourth, fifth and sixth term of the Arithmetic Progression so formed.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Determine the distance of the 8th round.

parts.label: (iii)(a)
parts.text: Find the total distance run after completing all 10 rounds. [OR (iii)(b): If a runner completes only the first 6 rounds, what is the total distance run by the runner?]

cases.text:
(i) a = 300, d = 50. Using aₙ = a + nd:
a₄ = 300 + 4 × 50 = 500 m, a₅ = 300 + 5 × 50 = 550 m, a₆ = 300 + 6 × 50 = 600 m.
(ii) a₈ = 300 + 8 × 50 = 700 m.
(iii)(a) Before finding the sum I checked my formula: with aₙ = a + nd the first round would be a₁ = 300 + 50 = 350 m, but the first round is 300 m. So aₙ = a + nd is wrong; the correct formula is aₙ = a + (n − 1)d. I will use the correct formula from here.
S₁₀ = (10/2)[2 × 300 + (10 − 1) × 50] = 5 × [600 + 450] = 5 × 1050 = 5250 m.

perStep.reason: DEPARTURE: wrong nth-term formula aₙ = a + nd adopted; a₄, a₅, a₆ = 500, 550, 600 (key 450, 500, 550) - 0 of 1 (MS 2025 041 30/1/1 Q36, PDF p16).
Still inside the departure: 300 + 8 × 50 uses the same wrong formula (value point is 300 + 7 × 50) - 0. Not ECF: (ii) re-applies a wrong METHOD, it does not carry a wrong VALUE.
700 m (key 650 m) - 0; the student never went back to correct (i) or (ii).
RETURN: the student explicitly abandons aₙ = a + nd and resumes the correct method; S₁₀ = (10/2)[2 × 300 + 9 × 50] matches the value point - 1.

commentMayMention: (i) and (ii) used aₙ = a + nd; the correct formula is aₙ = a + (n − 1)d
the student noticed the error in (iii) and used the correct formula there
expected.examinerNote: Departure that RETURNS. The wrong formula is adopted and worked from through (i) and (ii) (owner/README convention 3; app ECF_POLICY_V2 (a)), then explicitly abandoned in (iii), where the correct method is resumed. A CBSE examiner marks each part as written: (i) 0, (ii) 0, (iii) 2 = 2/4. The departure zone (steps 1-3) earns 0; everything after the return earns normally. A grader that zeroes positionally and never releases the departure gives 0/4 (August defect 9); one that credits (i)/(ii) because the student later stated the right formula gives 3-4/4 - both wrong. Type: wrong formula = method misunderstood = conceptual (knowledge gap); the later self-check does not repair (i)/(ii). Tolerance: none expected; ECF does not apply to (ii) because (ii) repeats the wrong method rather than carrying a wrong value.

question.text: In our homes, we receive the supply of electric power through a main supply also called mains, either supported through overhead electric poles or by underground cables. In our country the potential difference between the two wires (live wire and neutral wire) of this supply is 220 V.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Write the colours of the insulation covers of the line wires through which supply comes to our homes.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: What should be the current rating of the electric circuit (220 V) so that an electric iron of 1 kW power rating can be operated?

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: What is the function of the earth wire? State the advantage of the earth wire in domestic electric appliances such as electric iron. [OR (c)(ii): List two precautions to be taken to avoid electrical accidents...]

scheme.valuePoint: Earth wire provides a low-resistance conducting path so leakage current flows to earth; body kept at earth potential
The user will not get an electric shock

cases.text:
(a) Live wire — red insulation; neutral wire — black insulation.
(b) P = 1 kW = 1000 W, V = 220 V.
P = V/I ⇒ I = V/P = 220/1000 = 0.22 A.
So a circuit of current rating 1 A would be enough for the iron.
Wait — this is wrong: power is P = V × I, not V/I (1 watt = 1 volt × 1 ampere). Ignore the two lines above. Redoing:
P = V × I ⇒ I = P/V = 1000 W / 220 V = 4.54 A.
So the circuit must have a current rating of 5 A.
(c)(i) The earth wire provides a low-resistance conducting path for current, so any current leaking to the metallic body of the iron flows to the earth and the body stays at the potential of the earth. Hence the user does not get an electric shock.

perStep.reason: After the RETURN: P = VI ⇒ I = 1000/220 = 4.54 A (value point). The withdrawn lines (P = V/I, I = 0.22 A) were explicitly cancelled by the student and are not assessed.
Current rating 5 A (value point); the withdrawn '1 A' line is not assessed.
Low-resistance path to earth; body kept at earth potential.
No electric shock to the user.

departure.note: Wrong law P = V/I adopted and worked from for two lines (I = 0.22 A, '1 A rating'), then explicitly withdrawn; the return redoes scheme steps 3-4, so the excursion leaves nothing behind.

source.question: Q24

question.text: An object is placed at a distance of 60 cm from a concave lens of focal length 30 cm. Use lens formula to find the position of the image formed in this case.

scheme.valuePoint: u = −60 cm, f = −30 cm; lens formula 1/f = 1/v − 1/u
1/v = −1/30 − 1/60 = −3/60 ⇒ v = −20 cm (image 20 cm from the lens, same side as object)

cases.text:
u = −90 cm, f = −30 cm (concave lens)
Lens formula: 1/f = 1/v − 1/u
1/(−30) = 1/v − 1/(−90)
1/v = −1/30 − 1/90 = (−3 − 1)/90 = −4/90 = −2/45
v = −45/2 = −22.5 cm
The image is formed 22.5 cm from the lens, on the same side as the object.

perStep.reason: Lens formula 1/f = 1/v − 1/u correctly stated - the MS's ½ on this line is for the formula (MS 2025 086 31/1/1 Q24, PDF p4); f = −30 cm correct.
u copied as −90 cm (the question gives 60 cm, a 6/9 misread) and substituted - the miscopy is penalised ONCE, here.
v = −22.5 cm follows correctly from the student's u (ECF: −1/30 − 1/90 = −4/90), with the correct interpretation (same side, virtual) - CBSE MS general instruction 10.

expected.studentHeading: Marks to gain — you already know this
commentMayMention: u was copied as 90 cm; the question gives 60 cm
the lens formula and the sign convention are correct
v = −22.5 cm follows correctly from u = −90 cm
modelAnswerKeyFacts: v = −20 cm (20 cm from the lens on the object side)
